training_protocol: Existing redundant83s paired bath/no-cue protocol. Cues40..50 and53..63; response windows41..46 and54..59; baseline/recovery30..40 and73..83. Physical sensory bath drives existing AWA pathway; no internal control pulses imposed.
objective: Regional joint angular-speed RMS from dense time/joint differences, normalized to matched no-cue window in tail/middle/head. Hinge reward toward increasing suppression; every region and both responses must meet target. Frequency and bend amplitude also recorded. This measures motion attenuation and can improve through slower oscillation and/or smaller bends; no claim of pure cadence slowing.
preservation: No-cue cycle amplitudes and joint angular-speed RMS90..110% of original baseline (cycle floor.003rad); frequency1.62..1.98Hz and within5% of reference. Cue-off active windows preserve baseline gait and movement, and cue-minus-sham regional rate residual <=max(1e-5,.25*target). Preserve AIYL headroom>=2%, q01>=.05, abs cue mean response>=2e-5, stable half-window sign, recovery and nonrailing. Safety unchanged. During cue, zero frequency/zero cycle amplitude permitted as rest progresses.
final_validation: One changed selected checkpoint at highest training-achieved rung (or1% if none), tested nominal, low-dose, shift, repeat, redundant close-repeat, long-cue, nominal neural-half, nominal body-half, sensory-blocked, AIYL no-cue release replay only on existing RIAL edge, and RIAL no-cue release replay on existing SMD outputs. Retain full raw in all11 final cases. Counterfactual matched no-cue replays are final diagnostics only.
criteria: All8 normal cases meet regional motion suppression plus safety, gait/recovery/relay preservation on same checkpoint. Sensory block removes cue-specific rate response within.25*target and AIYL change within5e-6. Grid differences <=.25*target. Both AIYL->RIAL and RIAL->SMD release replays must reduce cue attenuation to<=25% of original while preserving baseline. These two probes have separate cache keys. Rest/restart component additionally requires>=95% rate reduction and cycle amplitudes<=10% baseline in all8 normal cases.
